# True iterative deepening: completed four-loop diagnostic

## Result and disposition

The registered two-level saved-proof curriculum completed and passed every
required all-root, All-native cold barrier, including the final original 58-query
geometry. It was negative: successful staged native-through-drain plus cold
guard time was **30.038 s versus 16.330 s** one-shot (+83.95%), before charging
three preventable harness mistakes. Final distinct native records increased
from 19,529 to 36,894 and domains from 35,510 to 52,872.

These are one concurrent exploratory comparison, not isolated qualification.
Reject this tested curriculum; do not start a five-loop staging transfer without
new evidence. This does not establish that every form of iterative deepening
fails. No engine, algebraic rule, owner payload or production checkpoint changed.

## What was actually tested

Evidence root: `TMP/codex-true-deepening.l9fXPO/`.
Machine ledger: `results.json`; preregistration: `deepening-plan.json`;
input proofs: `inputs/receipt.json`; actual argv: `commands/*.json`.

The earlier proxy put 16 finite Auxiliary shells before 58 Required rows and
admitted all 74 before traversal. It had no completed-scope barrier or saved-proof
feedback; its 28.89% loss did not test genuine staging.

This experiment instead used the already-generated reindexed 16-owner library
and 508 routes unchanged, with real native checkpoint/resume:

1. One-shot control: all 90 rows at once.
2. Fresh stage 0: 16 finite Required corner shells, 97 entry points; cold-All PASS.
3. Authenticated amendment 1: 16 containing finite shells, 1,456 entry points;
   resume the same saved proof; cold-All PASS.
4. Authenticated amendment 2: all 58 original full-scope row objects/IDs verbatim;
   resume again; cold-All plus exact original 58 coverage PASS.

Both final arms have exactly 90 rows: 16 Required and 74 Auxiliary. Public
amendments assign new queries Auxiliary, so the original 58 are Auxiliary in
both arms. Their external geometric scope is unchanged and independently
verified. This is **not** qualification of the production 116-Required scope.
Finite caps apply only to entry shells; native descendants retain their normal
translated bounds and are not clipped. The feedback is retained graph, records,
lookup and G2 proof, not regenerated algebra.

The actual protected initial prefix differs: 64 admitted representatives in
one-shot versus 16 retained across staged resumes. This is the available
authenticated staged-admission mechanism, not an isolated rank comparator.

## Costs, mechanism and failed setup attempts

Successful intrinsic native time totals 13.294877 s staged versus 7.820014 s
one-shot. Guarded native + cold totals 30.038061 s versus 16.329673 s. Successful
native CPU was 25.991376 s versus 18.009750 s; cold CPU 51.389618 s versus 36.411869 s.
Peak sampled native process-tree RSS was 342,691,840 B staged versus 278,147,072 B
one-shot; per-child RSS and cold RSS remain separately recorded in `results.json`.

Stage 1 reused the lower proof and added only 2,526 native records, but the final
expansion still added 19,432—nearly the entire 19,529-native one-shot workload.
Thus the lower stages did not repay their added work. Summed coordinator
inspection wall was 4.952860 s staged versus 4.275975 s one-shot; restore 1.032689 s
versus approximately 0; checkpoint 0.056910 s versus 0.021317 s. Repeated preparation
and cold barriers add further cost. The three successful staged cold passes
reinspected 69,292 records in total. These observations support rejecting this
curriculum, without attributing all change uniquely to rank or to the scheduler.

Three preventable harness errors were exposed by actual execution despite the
source being available beforehand. None was silently converted into a native
closure failure or omitted from cost:

1. `runs/stage0`: native 4/`preparation_error` and cold 4/missing manifest.
   The adapter had not created `runs/staged`, while Epoch
   `walking/epoch/checkpoint/publication.rs:123` uses `fs::create_dir` for its
   checkpoint directory. Root authorized creating only that missing parent;
   the retry used fresh receipts and the same clock.
2. `runs/stage1`: native 2/usage error, no native output or checkpoint change.
   The planned argv wrongly treated `--resume` as Boolean. Public
   `cli/args/owner_match.rs:345` and `:399` require `--resume DIR`, mutually
   exclusive with `--checkpoint`. A private adapter copy changed exactly one
   assertion; fresh corrected argv retained the original checkpoint and chain.
   Shared adapters used by P2 were not modified.
3. `runs/stage1-retry/cold.json`: PASS was only PhysicsQueries because automatic
   cold scope switches after amendments. The strict barrier checker rejected
   it. Fresh cold-only receipts explicitly set `--certification-scope all-roots`;
   final stage 2 used that explicit mode from the outset.

Failed native through-drain cost 2.214242 s, failed cold 1.160226 s, and insufficient
Physics-only cold 3.154160 s add 6.528629 s. Including those attempts gives staged
guarded native + cold 36.566690 s. Including native admission/recorder overhead too
gives 41.142864 s staged versus 16.559338 s one-shot. Full wall protocol time at
drain was 738.505 s, including control, human/tool coordination and correction
audits; it is not substituted for a clean matched solver timing. Reporting
also remained within the unchanged 1800 s ceiling.

## Exact execution and evidence

The authoritative native argv are JSON arrays; the runner invokes them unchanged.
Successful arrays were `commands/one-shot.json`, `stage0-retry.json`,
`stage1-retry.json`, and `stage2-corrected.json`. Cold arrays have corresponding
`-cold.json` for the first two and `-cold-all-roots.json` for the latter two.
Original failed arrays and outputs are retained, not overwritten.

The actual invocation pattern was:

```bash
PILOT_PYTHON=/nix/store/2dkfxh789byan1h81sjhjzsijjsfb57m-python3-3.11.15-env/bin/python3
PILOT_STUDY=/common/dev/rustred/TMP/codex-true-deepening.l9fXPO
PILOT_SOURCE=/common/dev/rustred/TMP/codex-parallel-campaign.oiPK29/repo

# This source was 3428 during execution; it has since advanced. Do not rerun
# these consumed output paths or restart the recorded clock.
# L=one-shot or stage0-retry: A=run_saved_step.py; C=cold.
# L=stage1-retry or stage2-corrected: A=run_saved_step-resume.py; C=cold-all-roots.
"$PILOT_PYTHON" -B "$PILOT_STUDY/$A" \
  --clock "$PILOT_STUDY/deepening-clock.json" --source "$PILOT_SOURCE" \
  --command "$PILOT_STUDY/commands/$L.json" \
  --evidence "$PILOT_STUDY/runs/$L/native-guard" \
  --cpus 32-47 --lock /common/dev/rustred/TMP/locks/pilot-d1.lock \
  --time-limit 180 --grace 30 --remaining-reserve 150
"$PILOT_PYTHON" -B "$PILOT_STUDY/with_deadline.py" guard \
  --clock "$PILOT_STUDY/deepening-clock.json" --cwd "$PILOT_SOURCE" \
  --command "$PILOT_STUDY/commands/$L-$C.json" \
  --evidence "$PILOT_STUDY/runs/$L/$C-guard" \
  --cpus 32-47 --lock /common/dev/rustred/TMP/locks/pilot-d1.lock \
  --phase-limit 90 --reserve 30
```

Each `prepare_stages.py check` named its actual cold file, stage 0 / 1 / 2, and the
unchanged `inputs` fixture (`--one-shot` for control stage 2). Only after PASS,
`prepare_stages.py append --stage 0/1` used the verified report to create
`amendments/1.json` or `2.json`; no private digest implementation was used.
Both amendment files are resupplied on final resume in sequence.

`setup-corrections-d1.json` and `cold-scope-correction-d1.json` pin every corrected
array and the one-line private adapter delta. `resource-amendment-d1.json` pins
the shared resource adapters; the original plan, clock and input pins never
changed. Independent critic reviewed resource parameters, both correction
deltas and the actual cold scope. The machine ledger carries per-phase receipt
hashes for independent acceptance.

D2 disposition: **not started; not recommended for this curriculum**. No further
deepening experiment or source change follows from this negative result.
